questions.question: What does component composition mean in React?

options.text: Putting the entire application into one component.
Combining smaller components to build more complex interfaces.
Replacing every component with an HTML file.
Editing the DOM directly for every update.

questions.explanation: Component composition builds interfaces from smaller components. Each component can focus on a specific responsibility and be reused.

questions.question: Which prop lets a Panel component render content nested inside <Panel>...</Panel>?
questions.explanation: React passes nested content through the children prop. Panel can place that content in its layout by rendering {children}.

questions.question: Two sibling components need to display and update the same selected course. What is a suitable approach?

options.text: Store separate, unrelated copies of the selection in both components.
Modify one sibling's props directly from the other.
Read the selected course from the DOM whenever it is needed.
Store the selection in their closest common parent and pass it down with update callbacks.

questions.explanation: Lifting state to a common parent gives both components a shared source of truth. Props provide the current value, and callbacks allow updates.

questions.question: Which update adds a new item to an array in React state without mutating the existing array?
questions.explanation: The spread syntax creates a new array containing the previous items and the new item. The functional updater uses the pending state.

questions.question: A route has the path /courses/:courseId. Which hook reads courseId inside the route's component?
questions.explanation: React Router's useParams hook returns the dynamic parameters matched in the URL, including courseId.

questions.question: Which element is intended for internal client-side navigation in a React Router application?
questions.explanation: Link navigates to an application route without requiring a full document reload during normal internal navigation.

questions.question: If package.json defines "build": "vite build", what does npm run build do?

options.text: Start the development server with hot module replacement.
Automatically push the project to GitHub.
Generate a production build, normally in the dist folder.

questions.explanation: vite build prepares production assets. The default output directory is dist. Publishing those files is a separate deployment step.

questions.question: An application is hosted at https://example.com/frontend_project/. Which Vite base value matches this deployment path?
questions.explanation: The base setting specifies the public base path used for asset URLs. Hosting under /frontend_project/ requires asset paths that match that location.
